sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store (never charged, never written to the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging, so it stays current and can take over again.
sonnet.q3: 7 days in a row with mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared (a failing day breaks the streak). A person makes the move.
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. This applies in both and new_only modes (not shadow).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only with all gates reset. The rollout must go through shadow again and meet the gates again, with the 7-day count starting from zero, before the new engine can charge again.
sonnet.q6: From day 35 in new_only, because the usage event log keeps events only 35 days and the old engine can only catch up on events still in the log. The count starts when new_only is entered.
sonnet.q8: Comparison evidence is in comparison_results (written by the nightly comparison job; gate checks read from it). What stops premature promotion: a move happens only when its gate is met and a person makes it. The document does not state how this is enforced; the rollout tool is not written yet.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate (share of charge attempts that fail) over 10-minute windows. When the rate exceeds 2% in both or new_only, it starts a rollback.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED. Only that pause_charging stops charging so no new charge goes out during the switch, and resume_charging has the old engine start charging again at the end. Handling of due charges is not described.
sonnet.q11: The reconcile step checks each customer and billing period against what has already been charged and written to the ledger, which stops a period from being charged twice (and stops a due charge from being dropped).
sonnet.q12: The state after a failed step is NOT STATED (and whether the flag holds rolling_back is an open question). The failed step can be retried; the rollback record shows which steps have finished, so the retry picks up at the step that failed.
